title: Supreme Court poised to side with Catholic preschools against Colorado
description: WASHINGTON, D.C. ( LifeSiteNews ) – A majority of U.S. Supreme Court justices indicated sympathy with Catholic parents and students on Tuesday in oral arguments over the state of Colorado’s attempts to exclude them from a universal preschool program on the basis of their schools’ opposition admitting children raised by homosexuals. As covered last year by LifeSiteNews, since 2022 Colorado’s universal preschool program (UPK) has enabled parents to send children to one of the top five preschools that they choose for free. But two preschools run by St. Mary Catholic Parish and St. Bernadette Catholic Parish were excluded from the program on the basis of their written commitment to uphold the Church’s moral teachings, including on gender and sexuality, which could conflict with admitting students from households that reject th … Left-wing Justice Sonia Sotomayor, by contrast, accused Sarah Harris, the attorney from the Trump Justice Department (which was siding with Becket and the religious schools) of “basically saying” that “we can exclude people merely because the exposure to them would cause us harm.” Harris countered that “requiring parents to agree with a school that they’re going to adhere to tenets of the Catholic faith and act consistently with them” was a straightforward exercise of religion, which is protected by the First Amendment. The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in 2022’s Carson v. Makin that a state-run program for tuition aid in Maine could not bar “sectarian” schools – religiously affiliated schools – from taking part, which would violate the free exercise of religion assured by the First Amendment. Vermont is currently embroiled in another controversy about excluding religious schools from tuition assistance.
